input.quote: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
input.rationale: IBM's indemnity in Section 8.1 covers third-party patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret claims relating to Materials and Base Components, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, the usual exclusions (Customer-provided items, Customer modifications, combinations, non-IBM items) and the usual remedies (continue use, modify, replace, credit), and indemnification payments are carved out of the liability cap by Section 9.1(a). That limb therefore sits at the playbook fallback (IP-only scope, credit capped at twelve months of charges, no breach-of-law/data-breach/gross-negligence limbs) and we do not redline it. The material failure is on the other side: Section 8.2(a)(3) makes us indemnify IBM against any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", i.e. a one-way customer indemnity for the vendor's own services, which is walk-away territory under this rule. Section 8.2(c) only relieves us where IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach caused the damages, so we remain exposed for IBM's ordinary negligence and service defects. The redline narrows 8.2(a)(3) to Content and our breach of applicable law and excludes claims arising from IBM's performance, matching the preferred position.

ops.oldText: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
ops.newText: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and arises out of Content or Customer's breach of applicable law, and not out of IBM's performance of the Services; or

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have narrowed our indemnity in Section 8.2(a)(3) so that it covers Services Recipient claims arising from Content or our breach of law, rather than any claim related directly or indirectly to IBM's Services. Our playbook keeps the customer indemnity limited to customer-provided content and customer breach of law, and we should not indemnify IBM for claims caused by its own performance; IBM's IP indemnity in Section 8.1 is otherwise acceptable as drafted.
proposal.summary: Narrow Customer's indemnity for Services Recipient claims to Content and Customer's breach of law, excluding claims arising from IBM's performance.
